title: (Scenario) A Kafka partition reassignment is triggered for scaling/rebalancing and you observe spikes in consumer lag and latency: explain the five causes: (1) data copying saturates disk I/O and network on source/destination brokers, (2) throttling slows replication but keeps the pipe busy longer, (3) leader movement causes consumers to reconnect (NOT_LEADER_FOR_PARTITION errors + metadata refresh), (4) cold page cache on the new broker forces disk reads instead of memory reads until cache warms, (5) coordination overhead from ISR changes and metadata propagation: and why you should monitor replication throughput, avoid reassignment during peak traffic, and throttle appropriately?
shortTitle: (Scenario) A partition reassignment for scaling/rebalancing causes spikes in consumer lag and latency: explain the five causes and how to mitigate them.

s1_definition.oneliner: Reassignment copies data online, so lag spikes come from disk and network saturation, throttling that trades rate for duration, leader moves that force metadata refresh, cold page cache on the destination, and coordination churn -- mitigate by monitoring replication throughput, avoiding peak hours, and throttling appropriately.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Bulk data copying** -- the destination broker fetches the entire partition log from the source, competing with normal traffic for disk and network.
- **Throttling trade-off** -- capping replication rate reduces instantaneous contention but extends how long the reassignment runs.
- **Leader movement** -- consumers get NOT_LEADER_FOR_PARTITION errors and must refresh metadata and reconnect.
- **Cold page cache** -- the new broker has none of the partition's data in memory, so reads hit disk until the cache warms.
- **Coordination overhead** -- ISR changes, leader elections, and metadata propagation add churn when many partitions move at once.
s1_definition.analogy: Imagine National Bank of India is relocating account records from one branch vault to another while the branch stays open. Moving boxes ties up the loading dock and trucks (disk/network saturation). To avoid blocking the dock, movers go slower but occupy it longer (throttling). Tellers told the ledger moved have to look up the new location (leader movement). At the new vault, clerks have not memorized where anything is (cold cache). And the manager keeps updating the master directory (coordination overhead).

sections.s3_flow:
```text
 Five Causes of Reassignment Lag Spikes
 ========================================

 Reassignment triggered
        │
        ▼
 ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ 1. DISK/NETWORK SATURATION                   │
 │    Destination copies entire partition log    │
 │    Competes with normal produce/consume       │
 ├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 │ 2. THROTTLING TRADE-OFF                      │
 │    Lower rate = less contention               │
 │    But longer duration of elevated load        │
 ├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 │ 3. LEADER MOVEMENT                           │
 │    NOT_LEADER_FOR_PARTITION errors            │
 │    Metadata refresh + reconnect               │
 ├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 │ 4. COLD PAGE CACHE                           │
 │    New broker: no data in memory              │
 │    Reads hit disk until cache warms            │
 ├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 │ 5. COORDINATION OVERHEAD                     │
 │    ISR changes, leader elections              │
 │    Metadata propagation to all brokers        │
 └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘

 Mitigations:
   Monitor replication throughput
   Avoid peak traffic hours
   Throttle appropriately
   Move in small batches
   Always run --verify to remove throttle
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
A partition reassignment is an online operation that moves replicas between brokers, but it causes transient lag and latency spikes for five reasons: disk and network saturation from bulk data copying, throttling that trades intensity for duration, leader movement forcing metadata refresh, cold page cache on the destination, and coordination overhead from ISR changes.

The mitigations map directly to these causes. Monitor replication throughput to detect saturation. Avoid peak traffic hours so spare capacity absorbs the impact. Throttle appropriately and move partitions in small batches so only a few clients see errors at once. Always run verify afterward to remove the throttle.

In my National Bank of India cluster, we saw settlement lag spike when we added brokers during peak hours. Moving in small batches off-peak with a throttle kept the impact minimal.

Remember one sentence: reassignment is safe and online but causes lag from five real causes, so plan it like any capacity-sensitive operation -- off-peak, throttled, in small batches, and always verify to clean up.

---

keyPoints: Bulk data copying during reassignment saturates disk and network, competing with normal traffic.
Throttling reduces contention but extends the duration of the reassignment.
Leader movement causes NOT_LEADER_FOR_PARTITION errors and brief metadata refresh latency.
Cold page cache on the new broker forces disk reads until the cache warms up.
Coordination overhead from ISR changes and metadata propagation adds churn at scale.
Always run --verify after reassignment to remove the throttle config; a forgotten throttle silently caps replication.
